findings.summary: The cart creates a 'PENDING' order, but the order state machine on the next order page has no PENDING state.
findings.evidence: Cart page: "Create a ==PENDING== order" and diagram edge "order" to "pay" labelled "PENDING". Order page: "CREATED → PAYMENT_PENDING → PLACED → ACCEPTED".
findings.fix: Use the state-machine names on the cart page. Say the cart creates an order in CREATED, which moves to PAYMENT_PENDING when payment is initiated, and relabel the diagram edge.

findings.summary: Geo partitioning is described with geohash cells, but the rest of the design (search, fallback list, pricing zones) uses H3 cells.
findings.evidence: "Geo partitioning: shard by ==city==, then by geohash cell" versus "H3 cell" in the search flow and "GET /pricing/zone/{h3}"
findings.fix: Change to "shard by city, then by H3 cell" so one geo index is used throughout.

findings.summary: Edge labels overlap node labels in the request flow diagram.
findings.evidence: "gRPC" overprints "CDN" under the CDN icon, and "sync" and "events" sit on top of the Order service and Payment service box borders.
findings.fix: Move the edge labels clear of the node labels and box borders, and add spacing between the CDN label and the gRPC arrow.

findings.summary: Geo partitioning is described with geohash cells, but geohash and H3 are only introduced later, and the rest of the design uses H3 for the same job.
findings.evidence: "shard by ==city==, then by geohash cell" vs later "H3 cell" in search, fallback and pricing.
findings.fix: Say "geo cell (geohash or H3, compared in the search chapter)" here, or use H3 consistently.

findings.summary: CDC is used in the catalog flow and diagram without ever being expanded or explained.
findings.evidence: "CDC publishes the change to Kafka" and diagram node "Kafka (CDC)", with no definition anywhere in the part.
findings.fix: Add a one-line definition at first use: change data capture, which streams committed DB row changes to Kafka without the app dual-writing.

findings.summary: The catalog page says the cart stores an item version, but the cart data model later stores only a priceSnapshot.
findings.evidence: Catalog: "Cart stores the version it saw, per item". Cart: "items[{itemId, qty, modifiers, priceSnapshot}]" with no item version.
findings.fix: Add the catalog item version to the cart item fields, or change the catalog text to say the cart compares priceSnapshot.

findings.summary: Reconciliation is described as daily on one line and as fixing a lost webhook within 15 minutes on another, so the cadence contradicts itself.
